_: Skylight: the hemisphere of scattered daylight (blue clear sky, white overcast). Values are luminances and illuminances on the ground plane; the angular distribution comes from a model (CIE standard skies, Perez, Preetham, Hosek-Wilkie, Prague). World lane 2026-11-07.

clear_sky_zenith_luminance_kcd_m2.src: E: recalled from IESNA / CIE lighting practice (CIE_LIGHTING), not re-read: CIE_LIGHTING: rises with sun elevation and turbidity; ~3-5 kcd/m2 at mid sun elevations (recalled)

clear_sky_horizon_vs_zenith.v: clear skies brighten toward the horizon (except opposite the sun) and around the sun (circumsolar aureole); darkest ~90 deg from the sun

overcast_luminance_kcd_m2.src: E: recalled from IESNA / CIE lighting practice (CIE_LIGHTING), not re-read: CIE_LIGHTING (recalled ranges)

cie_overcast_distribution.v: L(theta) = L_z (1 + 2 cos theta) / 3: zenith 3x the horizon (theta from zenith)

diffuse_horizontal_illuminance_klx.src: E: recalled from IESNA / CIE lighting practice (CIE_LIGHTING), not re-read: CIE_LIGHTING typical daylight values (recalled)

cct_K.src: E: recalled from IESNA / CIE lighting practice (CIE_LIGHTING), not re-read: CIE_LIGHTING (photographic practice; recalled)

spectrum_reference.v: CIE D65 (and D50/D75 family) for daylight composites; clear blue sky ~ Rayleigh lambda^-4 shaped; full-spectral models: Hosek-Wilkie 2012 (BSD-3 code), Prague 2021 (colour-science BSD-3); see light.sun spectral_table for D65

v.CIE_standard_general_sky: 15 types (overcast to clear), luminance ratios only (CIE_S011)
v.Perez_all_weather: 5-parameter luminance distribution from clearness and brightness (PEREZ93)
v.Preetham: analytic, turbidity T 2-10; known too-bright/saturated at low sun
v.Hosek_Wilkie: fitted spectral radiance, turbidity 1-10, ground albedo; code BSD-3
v.Prague: full atmosphere incl. altitude and low sun; colour-science BSD-3

note.v: a light source: no material surface

golden_hour.src: ANON_E: warm sun + blue sky shadows

CIE_D65.cite: CIE (2019) CIE standard illuminant D65. International Commission on Illumination, Vienna. doi:10.25039/CIE.DS.hjfjmt59 (ISO/CIE 11664-2:2022 Table B.1). Fetched 11-07 from files.cie.co.at/Publications-datasets/CIE_std_illum_D65.csv
CIE_D65.lic: CC BY-SA 4.0 (dataset metadata, 11-07): attribution given here; the 33-value excerpt is ShareAlike - keep this attribution with it. Re-checked 11-08: the D65 data page now shows only 'Copyright CIE' and its metadata JSON is not reachable (404); a CIE CSV metadata record (another dataset) states CC BY-SA 4.0. BY-SA permits commercial use with attribution and ShareAlike, so not STUDY ONLY under P13; the ShareAlike duty travels with the excerpt

ASTMG173.cite: ASTM G173-03 (reapproved 2020) Standard Tables for Reference Solar Spectral Irradiances: Direct Normal and Hemispherical on 37 deg Tilted Surface (AM1.5; SMARTS 2.9.2). Global integrates to 1000.4 W/m2, direct 900.1 W/m2. Point values read 11-07 from the NREL-distributed table as copied in pvlib-python (pvlib/data/ASTMG173.csv)
ASTMG173.lic: ASTM copyright on the standard document; the data are distributed free by NREL (US government) and pvlib (BSD-3-Clause); 33 point values used as facts

KOPP11.cite: Kopp G, Lean JL. A new, lower value of total solar irradiance: evidence and climate significance. Geophys Res Lett 38:L01706 (2011): TSI 1360.8 +/- 0.5 W/m2

DARULA05.cite: Darula S, Kittler R, Gueymard CA. Reference luminous solar constant and solar luminance for illuminance calculations. Solar Energy 79:559-565 (2005): luminous solar constant 133.8 klx. Recalled

CIE_S011.cite: CIE S 011/E:2003 (ISO 15469:2004) Spatial distribution of daylight - CIE standard general sky (15 sky types); CIE standard overcast sky L(theta) = Lz (1 + 2 cos theta)/3 (Moon & Spencer 1942)
CIE_S011.lic: CIE standard, copyright; the formulas used as facts

PEREZ93.cite: Perez R, Seals R, Michalsky J. All-weather model for sky luminance distribution: preliminary configuration and validation. Solar Energy 50:235-245 (1993)

PREETHAM99.cite: Preetham AJ, Shirley P, Smits B. A practical analytic model for daylight. SIGGRAPH 1999

HOSEK12.cite: Hosek L, Wilkie A. An analytic model for full spectral sky-dome radiance. ACM TOG 31(4) (SIGGRAPH 2012); reference code ArHosekSkyModel (as shipped in Blender intern/sky and OSPRay)
HOSEK12.lic: code BSD-3-Clause (Blender/OSPRay SPDX headers; checked by search 11-07): usable commercially with attribution

WILKIE21.cite: Wilkie A, Vevoda P, Bashford-Rogers T, et al. A fitted radiance and attenuation model for realistic atmospheres (Prague Sky Model). ACM TOG 40(4) (2021); implementation in colour-science (BSD-3-Clause)

CIE_LIGHTING.cite: General daylight / lighting-engineering figures (IESNA Lighting Handbook 10th ed.; CIE 085 / CIE 13.3-1995 colour rendering; EBU Tech 3355 TLCI-2012): sky luminances, illuminances, CCTs. Recalled typical ranges
CIE_LIGHTING.lic: EBU Tech 3355 free; IES handbook copyright; typical numbers used as facts

ANON_E.cite: Estimate made in this lane; the reason is given in each src
